# Sirach Chapter 4 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 4 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_004_page_001.jpg

---

1 My child, do not rob the poor of their living, and do not keep the needy waiting in suspense.

2 Do not add to the grief of the hungry, nor provoke a person who is already in distress.

3 Do not make a troubled heart more bitter, nor delay giving to one who is in need.

4 Do not reject the appeal of the afflicted, and do not turn your face away from the poor.

5 Do not avert your eyes from the needy, and give no one reason to curse you.

6 For if someone curses you out of bitterness, his Maker will hear his prayer.

7 Gain the goodwill of the assembly; before a person of influence, show deference.

8 Lend your ear to the poor, and answer them with a gentle word.

9 Rescue the wronged from their oppressor, and do not be cowardly in giving judgment.

10 Be like a father to orphans, and as a husband to their mother; then you will be like a child of the Most High, and he will love you more than a mother loves her child.

11 Wisdom nurtures her own children and cares for those who seek her.

12 Whoever loves her loves life, and those who seek her from early on will be filled with joy.

13 Whoever holds fast to her obtains glory, and the Lord blesses the house she enters.

14 Those who serve her serve the Holy One; the Lord loves those who love her.

15 Whoever obeys her will give judgment among the nations, and whoever heeds her will live in peace.

16 If he trusts her, he will inherit her; his descendants will hold her as their possession.

17 At first she will lead him along winding paths, bringing him fear and timidity, testing him with her rules until she trusts him fully.

18 Then she will return to him on the straight way and restore his joy, revealing her secrets to him.

19 But if he goes astray, she will abandon him and hand him over to his ruin.

20 Watch for the opportune time and guard yourself from evil; do not be ashamed of your whole self.

21 For some shame leads to sin, and there is shame that leads to honor and favor.

22 Do not favor anyone to your own harm, nor show deference to anyone that will bring you down.

23 Do not hesitate to speak at the right moment, and do not conceal your wisdom.

24 For wisdom is recognized through speech, and instruction through the words of the tongue.

25 Do not contradict the truth; acknowledge your ignorance honestly.

26 Do not be ashamed to confess your sins, and do not try to stop a river with your hand.

27 Do not defer to a foolish person, and show no favoritism to a person of influence.

28 Fight to the death for truth, and the Lord God will fight on your behalf.

29 Do not be rash in your tongue, and do not be slack and lax in your deeds.

30 Do not be like a lion in your own house, and do not be suspicious toward your household.

31 Do not let your hand be open to receive and closed when it is time to give.
